subject: Resilience sanity sweep + ops ownership handoff (post-deploy)
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-29T22:45:00Z
Subject: Resilience sanity sweep + ops ownership handoff (post-deploy)

Hi Sonia / EdgeOps team,

Congrats again on the deployment window — quick note to propose a short resilience sanity sweep tonight (after steady-state traffic stabilizes) and to confirm ops ownership handoff timelines. Our goal is to run a focused set of non-invasive checks that validate routing, KV cache priming, and failover behavior, then hand a concise ops packet to your SREs.

Planned checks (30-45 min):
- BGP path validation across two transit peers (confirm AS_PATH, prep for failover)
- MTU and checksum spot checks on the east-west fabric
- KV cache priming: run the prepop script and capture warmup stats (target > 70% cache hit for common prefixes)
- Health probe confirmation for the inference gateway (TLS cert, 200 on /healthz, latency sample)
- Controlled worker reboot on a non-primary replica to validate autoscaling and session rehydration

Attachments: ops-smoke-runbook-v1.pdf (run steps + rollback hints), kvcache-warmup-log.txt (template for logs we collect).

Requesting a single point of contact from your side for the handoff and escalation: is Sonia OK? If so, we can start at 23:15 UTC.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Platform Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

I'll be the POC and will have one EdgeOps engineer on the bridge (thanks for looping laura).

Thanks Sonia — answers inline and a small update to the runbook attached.

1) KV warmup timeline: prepop script runs in two phases (index & hot-prefixes). Expect ~6-9 minutes to reach ~60-70% for hot prefixes on the worker pool we primed; full warmup (cold prefixes) may take 25-35 minutes depending on traffic. We added an automated histogram capture in section 3 of the runbook so your alerting can use the 10-minute window sample.

2) Controlled reboot target: worker-id rw-az2-wk-13 (non-primary). We'll annotate the reboot in the bridge and fall back traffic to rw-az1 if needed.

Small clarifications to monitoring thresholds (added to runbook):
- Latency SLO for the gateway: p95 < 120ms over 5m window (post-warmup), degrade alert at p95 >= 200ms
- Health probe: /healthz responds 200 with JSON {"ready":true} — we included curl examples

Start time still 23:15 UTC. We'll collect these artifacts: kvcache-warmup-log.txt, small sample of gateway traces, and a screenshot of the bridge topology if we need to escalate (attached as bridge-screenshot.png).

If anything unexpected happens, tag the Slack channel #prod-onprem and escalate to laura_bennett@redwood.com — she's owning net fabric followups.

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T03:12:00Z
Subject: Post-sweep snapshot: passes, residual actions, and handoff

All — quick post-sweep readout. Short summary of what we observed, artifacts attached.

Outcome: PASS (no customer-impacting regressions observed)

What we ran and results:
- BGP validation: both transit peers present; one learned a longer AS_PATH for the backup path which we accepted for now. No route flaps during the window. (Artifact: BGP-table-sample.txt)
- MTU checks: east-west spot checks returned expected MTU 1500 across fabric. No fragmentation observed in 30s pings.
- KV cache priming: prepop phases completed. Observed warmup: 7 minutes to 65% hot-prefix hit; 28 minutes to 92% overall warm footprint under sample traffic. kvcache-warmup-log.txt attached.
- Gateway health: /healthz returned ready JSON and p95 latency settled to 98ms after warmup. Degrade threshold not hit.
- Controlled reboot (rw-az2-wk-13): graceful drain succeeded; health returned within 45s; autoscaling added replacement and no request errors.

Residual actions (low priority):
1) KVM: schedule a planned test for cross-AZ failover with a larger traffic spike (RINF-5423).
2) Update the runbook to include the BGP backup path note and expected AS_PATH length for troubleshooting.
3) Add a short command to the runbook that collects kernel dmesg on a reboot within the 60s window (useful for future root-cause).

Handoff: Sonia/EdgeOps, we attached a concise ops packet (ops-smoke-runbook-v1.pdf) and the logs. You're set for day-2 ownership. If you want us to stay on a 30-minute watch for the next business day, say the word and we'll extend coverage.

Thanks everyone — clean sweep.

Laura Bennett
Network Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
